metadata.title: Oracle breaks ground on $4.5bn headquarters in Nashville

content.text:
Oracle has begun construction of its planned $4.5bn global headquarters on Nashville's East Bank in Tennessee, US, marking a major development for the city's technology sector.
The company held a groundbreaking ceremony to signal the start of work on the site, which is intended to house engineering, technical, and healthcare technology workers in the coming years.
The event drew company executives, including Oracle CEOs Mike Sicilia and Clay Magouyrk, along with Tennessee Governor Bill Lee, Nashville Mayor Freddie O'Connell, Deputy Governor Stuart McWhorter, Governor-elect Marsha Blackburn, and US Senator Bill Hagerty.
Magouyrk said: "Today's groundbreaking is an important next step in our commitment to Nashville. We're grateful to the city, its leaders, and the community for welcoming and helping us reach today's critical milestone for our future campus."
Oracle's development represents a long-term investment in both the city and state economies.
The company's plans call for an HQ complex spanning approximately 78 acres, including 23 buildings with a combined 759,838ft² of office space.
The campus will feature various amenities, including retail units, a 120-room Nobu hotel and restaurant, green spaces, an amphitheatre, a six-acre lake, and a network of walking paths. The first buildings are expected to open by 2030.
As part of its investment, Oracle has allocated $175m for public infrastructure improvements.
This includes funding for an approximately 860ft pedestrian bridge across the Cumberland River, a public park, greenway connections, and road upgrades.
Designed by Foster + Partners, the campus will transform a former industrial site, with plans to plant over 1,900 trees, create ecological zones to support biodiversity, and seek LEED Gold certification.
Oracle aims to use the new campus to accelerate hiring, with expectations to create thousands of jobs during the development period.
The company's Nashville workforce includes professionals in engineering, sales, healthcare technology, marketing, and other areas.
Lee said: "Oracle's decision to build its global headquarters in Nashville reflects the strength of Tennessee's workforce and business-friendly climate. This investment will create high-quality jobs and new opportunities for Tennesseans to build their futures right here at home."
In support of the local community, Oracle has awarded $1.55m to Trinity Community Commons for property renovations and $150,000 in grants to 30 local nonprofits through its employee-directed programme.
The organisation also announced a $10m partnership with the Nashville Symphony, enabling the Symphony to resume its 2026-27 season.
"Oracle breaks ground on $4.5bn headquarters in Nashville" was originally created and published by World Construction Network, a GlobalData owned brand.
